text: {"brief_summary":"Example Trading LLC (synthetic) has about 220 employees across a head office in Dubai, a branch in Abu Dhabi and a warehouse in Jebel Ali. Today staff request leave by email or paper forms. HR keeps balances in Excel and spends about two days each month reconciling them before payroll. Managers often approve leave without seeing who else is away. The company wants: online requests for annual, sick, unpaid and compassionate leave, including from phones; manager approval with a team calendar; HR access to view and correct all requests and balances; balances calculated under UAE labour law and visible to employees; and monthly reports for HR and finance before payroll. Some warehouse shift staff have no company email accounts. Constraints: the company uses Microsoft 365 with company sign-in. Payroll is a separate system, and its vendor has not confirmed whether it offers an API. The first version should be live within three months. The internal IT team is two people, the budget is limited, and both Arabic and English are used.","technology_stack":{"title":"Technology stack for the leave management solution","question":"Which platform should the leave management solution be built on or configured in?","context":"The brief does not name a leave technology. Facts from the brief: the company already uses Microsoft 365 with company sign-in, the IT team is two people, the budget is limited, and the first version is due within three months. Users need phone access, and both Arabic and English are used. Balances must follow UAE labour law. Payroll is a separate system with no confirmed API. Some warehouse staff have no company email accounts. Assumption: the IT team has general Microsoft 365 administration skills but no professional software development capacity.","options":[{"key":"power_platform","title":"Microsoft Power Platform on Microsoft 365","description":"A Power Apps app (usable on phones and inside Teams) with data in SharePoint lists or Dataverse. Power Automate runs approvals and notifications, a shared calendar or Power BI view shows team absence, and Excel or Power BI covers monthly reports.","pros":["Uses the existing Microsoft 365 sign-in and tenant, so there is no new identity system","Approvals can arrive in Teams and Outlook, where managers already work","Low-code, so a two-person IT team can learn to make small changes","Can stay inside existing licences if limited to SharePoint and standard connectors","Realistic to deliver a first version within three months"],"cons":["UAE leave rules (accrual, sick-leave pay tiers, carry-over) must be built and maintained as custom logic","Warehouse staff without accounts would need Microsoft 365 accounts (for example frontline licences), which adds cost","Arabic right-to-left layout in Power Apps takes extra design effort","Dataverse or premium connectors would require extra per-user licences"]},{"key":"hr_saas","title":"Configured HR or leave management SaaS for the UAE market","description":"Subscribe to an existing HR or leave product that supports UAE leave rules, Arabic and English, and mobile apps. Configure it and connect sign-in to Microsoft 365 where the product supports that.","pros":["UAE leave rules and mobile apps are often available out of the box","Arabic and English support is usually already built in","Some products offer phone-number sign-in for staff without email","Vendor maintains the product, which reduces load on the two-person IT team","Some products include payroll export formats"],"cons":["Per-employee subscription for about 220 staff is an ongoing cost against a limited budget","Product selection and contracting can consume part of the three-month window","Less flexibility to fit company-specific policies or reports","Data is held by a third party, so data location and contract terms need review","May not integrate with the existing payroll system"]},{"key":"custom_azure","title":"Custom web application on Microsoft Azure","description":"A purpose-built responsive web application hosted on Azure, with sign-in through Microsoft Entra ID and a database for requests and balances.","pros":["Full control over leave rules, bilingual interface and reports","Can support accounts outside Microsoft 365 for warehouse staff","No per-user platform licence for the app itself"],"cons":["Highest build cost and longest delivery; hard to fit in three months","A two-person IT team would struggle to maintain custom code","Hosting, security and updates become an ongoing responsibility"]}],"recommended_option":"power_platform","recommendation_rationale":"Facts from the brief favour Power Platform: the company already uses Microsoft 365 with company sign-in, the budget is limited, IT capacity is two people, and the timeline is three months. Power Platform reuses the existing tenant and puts approvals in tools managers already use. If built on SharePoint and standard connectors, it may avoid new licence costs. The main weakness is that UAE leave rules must be built and maintained by the project. If the answers on warehouse access and leave rules show these are hard to meet, hr_saas should be reconsidered. This is a recommendation for discussion, not a decision.","assumptions":["The existing Microsoft 365 licences include Power Apps and Power Automate with standard connectors","The IT team can take over day-to-day administration of a low-code app after handover","About 220 users and their leave volumes fit within SharePoint list limits if Dataverse is not used","Warehouse staff can be given some form of Microsoft 365 identity at acceptable cost"],"risks":["Leave calculation logic built in Power Automate may be complex and error-prone without careful testing against UAE labour law","Licence costs for warehouse staff accounts may change the cost comparison with SaaS","Arabic right-to-left support may be weaker than expected for staff who prefer Arabic","Payroll integration may stay manual if the vendor has no API"],"source_quotes":["The company already uses Microsoft 365, and staff sign in with company accounts.","The internal IT team is two people, and the budget is limited.","Warehouse staff work in shifts; some of them do not have company email accounts."]},"delivery_approach":{"title":"Delivery approach","question":"How should the solution be delivered and rolled out to the three sites within the three-month target?","context":"Fact: the first version should be live within three months. The company has three locations (Dubai head office, Abu Dhabi branch, Jebel Ali warehouse), and warehouse staff work shifts and partly lack company accounts. Fact: payroll integration is uncertain because the vendor has not confirmed an API. Assumption: not every requested feature has to be in the first version, but the brief does not say which ones are essential.","options":[{"key":"phased_mvp","title":"Phased MVP, then increments","description":"Release a first version within three months covering online requests, manager approval with team calendar, balances under the agreed leave rules, HR correction, and a basic monthly report or export. Include a short pilot with one head-office team before go-live. Later increments add payroll integration, richer reports and other improvements.","pros":["Fits the three-month target by limiting first-version scope","Delivers the main pain points early: email and use"],"cons":["Requires the customer to agree on what is in and out of the first version","HR may run some manual steps (for example payroll handover) for a while","Several releases mean more change can be done site by site"],"cons":["Two systems (new tool and Excel) run in parallel during rollout, which may increase HR reconciliation work","The company-wide go-live may fall outside three months","Team calendars are incomplete while only some staff use the tool"]},{"key":"single_release","title":"Single release to all sites","description":"Build all requested features, including reports and any payroll link, and switch all 220 employees over on one date.","pros":["One cut-over date with no parallel running","All staff have the same process from day one"],"cons":["High risk of missing the three-month target given the payroll uncertainty","Any error in balance calculations affects everyone at once","Warehouse access must be fully solved before anyone can go live"]}],"recommended_option":"phased_mvp","recommendation_rationale":"The three-month target, the unconfirmed payroll API and a two-person IT team point to a limited first version that fixes the main problems the brief names: email and paper requests, managers not seeing who is away, and Excel reconciliation. A short pilot inside the first phase reduces risk without the long parallel running of a site-by-site rollout. Payroll integration and further reports can follow once the vendor's position is known. This is a proposal; the first-version scope needs agreement from the project's decision makers.","assumptions":["A file export or report for payroll is acceptable in the first version instead of a direct integration","HR can provide confirmed leave rules and opening balances early enough to test before go-live","One head-office team is available to pilot for one to two weeks"],"risks":["Scope disagreements about the first version could use up the three-month window","Opening balances from Excel may contain errors that surface at go-live","Warehouse access may not be ready for the first release if account decisions are late"],"source_quotes":["The first version should be live within three months.","Payroll runs on a separate system; the vendor has not confirmed whether it offers an API.","HR spends about two days each month reconciling balances"]},"clarifying_questions":[{"category":"users_and_roles","title":"Access for warehouse staff without company accounts","question":"How should warehouse staff who have no company email account request leave and see their balances?","why_it_matters":"The brief says staff sign in with company accounts but also that some warehouse staff have none. The answer affects licence costs, the platform choice and whether employees can see their own balances.","suggested_answers":[{"key":"frontline_accounts","title":"Give them Microsoft 365 frontline accounts","description":"Each warehouse employee gets a low-cost Microsoft 365 account and uses the app on their phone."},{"key":"supervisor_on_behalf","title":"Supervisor submits on their behalf","description":"A shift supervisor or HR enters requests for them; employees see balances on request or on a printout."},{"key":"shared_kiosk","title":"Shared device at the warehouse","description":"A tablet or PC at the warehouse lets staff submit requests using an employee number and PIN."},{"key":"separate_login","title":"Separate login without email","description":"Staff sign in by phone number or employee ID, which usually requires a SaaS product or custom build."}],"recommended_answer":"frontline_accounts","recommendation_rationale":"The brief requires balances to be visible to employees and online requests from phones. Individual accounts support both and keep a clear record of who requested what. Who will confirm the rules in writing?","why_it_matters":"Balance calculations are the core of the system. Accrual in the first year, carry-over, sick-leave pay tiers, probation, compassionate leave entitlement and unpaid leave effects must be defined before they can be built and tested.","suggested_answers":[{"key":"statutory_only","title":"Statutory minimum only","description":"Apply UAE labour law entitlements with no company-specific additions."},{"key":"written_company_policy","title":"Written company policy, checked against the law","description":"HR provides the company leave policy, reviewed against UAE labour law, as the single source for the rules."},{"key":"excel_as_reference","title":"Follow current Excel practice","description":"Rebuild the rules HR currently applies in the Excel workbook."}],"recommended_answer":"written_company_policy","recommendation_rationale":"A written, reviewed policy gives a testable reference. It also avoids copying errors or undocumented practice from the Excel workbook into the new system.","source_quotes":["Balances are calculated according to UAE labour law and visible to employees.","HR keeps balances in an Excel workbook."]},{"category":"integrations","title":"Payroll handover in the first version","question":"What should the first version provide to payroll, given the vendor has not confirmed an API?","why_it_matters":"A direct integration could take much of the three-month window or prove impossible. A file or report keeps the plan realistic but leaves a manual step.","suggested_answers":[{"key":"file_export","title":"Monthly file export","description":"The system produces a file in the format payroll can import, or that HR enters manually."},{"key":"report_only","title":"Report only","description":"HR and finance receive a monthly report and update payroll by hand."},{"key":"api_integration","title":"Direct API integration","description":"Connect to payroll directly, only if the vendor confirms an API in time."}],"recommended_answer":"file_export","recommendation_rationale":"The vendor has not confirmed an API and the first version is due within three months. A file export still reduces reconciliation work and can be replaced by an API link later.","source_quotes":["Payroll runs on a separate system; the vendor has not confirmed whether it offers an API.","Monthly leave reports for HR and the finance team, ready before payroll."]},{"category":"data","title":"Opening balances and history from Excel","question":"What should be moved from the Excel workbook into the new system at go-live?","why_it_matters":"Employees will see their balances from day one, so wrong opening balances undermine trust. Migrating history adds effort and risk.","suggested_answers":[{"key":"opening_balances","title":"Validated opening balances only","description":"HR confirms each employee's balance at a cut-over date, and only those figures are imported."},{"key":"current_year_history","title":"Opening balances plus current-year requests","description":"Import balances and this year's taken leave for reference."},{"key":"full_history","title":"Full history","description":"Import all past leave records from Excel."}],"recommended_answer":"opening_balances","recommendation_rationale":"This is common practice for short timelines. It keeps migration small, and HR validation catches errors before employees see their balances.","source_quotes":["HR keeps balances in an Excel workbook."]},{"category":"business_rules","title":"Working patterns for shift staff","question":"How should leave days be counted for staff who work shifts or different weekly patterns across the three sites?","why_it_matters":"Whether leave is counted in calendar days, working days or shifts, and which days are rest days or public holidays, changes balance calculations and may require roster data.","suggested_answers":[{"key":"pattern_per_site","title":"Fixed working pattern per site or group","description":"Define a standard working week and public holiday calendar per site or employee group."},{"key":"roster_based","title":"Based on individual shift rosters","description":"Leave is counted against each employee's actual roster, which needs roster data to be maintained."},{"key":"calendar_days","title":"Calendar days for all","description":"Count all leave in calendar days regardless of shifts."}],"recommended_answer":null,"recommendation_rationale":"","source_quotes":["Warehouse staff work in shifts; HR sees and can correct everything; a delegate is set when the manager is away."},{"key":"manager_then_hr","title":"Line manager, then HR","description":"Every request needs both manager and HR approval."},{"key":"by_leave_type","title":"Depends on leave type","description":"For example, annual leave needs manager approval only, while sick or unpaid leave also needs HR approval or documents."}],"recommended_answer":"manager_only","recommendation_rationale":"The brief describes managers approving or rejecting and HR seeing and correcting all requests.
